mainTopic: Giving each altar-fire verse its job: returning burned parts, the extra arrangement on יום הכיפורים, and why the fire for the קטורת, the מנורה and the מחתה comes from the outer altar
overview: This amud continues the discussion of the wood arrangements (מערכות) on the outer altar, especially on יום הכיפורים, and gives each verse about the altar fire its own job. First a ברייתא finishes teaching that limbs not yet burned go back on the altar, or wait on the כבש or סובב until the large arrangement is made. רבי מאיר uses that same verse to teach that partly burned parts of an עולה are returned to the altar, but partly burned קטורת is not, and a ברייתא from the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב supports him. Next the גמרא notes that all opinions agree on an extra arrangement on יום הכיפורים, learned from the extra letters in ״והאש״. A ברייתא then teaches from ״אש תמיד״ that the arrangement for the קטורת coals must be on the outer altar. The ברייתא asks where the fire for the מנורה and the מחתה comes from. Each time it tries a logical comparison, then shows that an opposite comparison is just as strong, so a פסוק is needed. ״אש תמיד״ fixes the מנורה's fire on the outer altar, and ״מלפני ה׳״ shows the מחתה's coals come from the outer altar too. Finally the גמרא begins to explain why that פסוק needs both ״מעל המזבח״ and ״מלפני ה׳״, and this explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Unburned limbs are arranged on the altar, or wait beside it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends its teaching. Limbs not finished burning go back on the altar. If there is no room, they wait on the ramp or ledge until the big arrangement is made, and then they are put on it. The source is ״אשר תאכל האש את העולה על המזבח״.
steps.simpleTranslation: [From where do we know about limbs that were not burned up] that we arrange them on the altar? And if the altar cannot hold them, we arrange them on the ramp or on the ledge until the large arrangement is made, and then we arrange them on it. The verse says: 'That which the fire will consume of the burnt-offering, on the altar.'
steps.whatsHappening: This amud opens in the middle of a ברייתא that the גמרא quoted just before. It finishes the teaching that leftover, unburned limbs must be returned to the altar fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says the fire 'will consume' the עולה 'on the altar.' The ברייתא reads this to mean that whatever the fire has started on must finish burning on the altar. If the altar is too crowded, the limbs may wait on the כבש or the סובב, but only until the next day's large arrangement is ready. This is how one view uses up this verse, so the verse cannot also be used to add another arrangement.

keyTerms.meaning: we arrange them (place them in order on the fire)
the ramp leading up to the outer altar
the ledge that runs around the middle of the altar
the large main wood arrangement on the altar
the verse teaches (introduces the source)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new discussion. It is the end of a ברייתא that started on the previous amud, so the opening words 'that they are arranged' finish the question 'from where do we know…?'

phrases.english: that they are arranged upon the altar,
and if [the altar] cannot hold them,
phrases.notes: Meaning there is not enough room on top of the altar.

phrases.english: that they are arranged upon the ramp
or upon the ledge,
until he makes the large arrangement, and then arranges them [on it]?
The verse states:

phrases.aramaic: ״אֲשֶׁר תֹּאכַל הָאֵשׁ אֶת הָעוֹלָה עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״.
phrases.english: 'That which the fire will consume of the burnt-offering, on the altar.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא begun on the previous amud, which explains how one view uses the verse ״אשר תאכל האש״.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unburned limbs from the evening go back on the altar. If there is no room, they wait on the כבש or סובב until the large arrangement is made.

steps.title: רבי מאיר uses the verse for returning partly burned offering parts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי מאיר does with this verse. He learns from it that partly burned parts of an עולה that fell off are returned, but partly burned קטורת is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר? [He learns:] Partly consumed parts of a burnt-offering, you return. But partly consumed incense, you do not return.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי מאיר and explains how he uses the same verse in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every תנא has to give each verse a job. רבי מאיר reads ״אשר תאכל האש את העולה״ as limited to the עולה. If partly burned parts of an עולה fall off the altar, they must be put back. Partly burned קטורת that fell off the inner altar is not put back.

keyTerms.meaning: partly consumed or burned remains
return (put back on the altar)
incense

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir [how does he use this verse]?
phrases.notes: A short question, answered right away in the next words.

phrases.english: Partly consumed parts of a burnt-offering you return,
but you do not return partly consumed incense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי מאיר's different reading of the same verse used in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does רבי מאיר learn from ״אשר תאכל האש את העולה על המזבח״?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: That partly burned parts of an עולה are returned to the altar, but partly burned קטורת is not.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי מאיר's reading
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנניא בר מניומי taught in the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב the same reading of the verse: partly burned עולה is returned, partly burned קטורת is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חנניא בר מניומי taught, in the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: 'That which the fire will consume of the burnt-offering, on the altar.' Partly consumed parts of a burnt-offering you return, but partly consumed incense you do not return.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that רבי מאיר's reading is a known, taught teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the exact same verse and states the exact same rule. This shows that רבי מאיר's use of the verse is grounded in an established source and is not invented just to answer the question. The key word is 'העולה': the verse is about the עולה, so קטורת is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: as he taught (introduces a ברייתא)
in the school of

phrases.english: As Rabbi Chananya bar Minyomi taught
in the school of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:

phrases.aramaic: ״אֲשֶׁר תֹּאכַל הָאֵשׁ אֶת הָעוֹלָה עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״ —
phrases.english: 'That which the fire will consume of the burnt-offering, on the altar' —
partly consumed parts of a burnt-offering you return,
but you do not return partly consumed incense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 2 with a ברייתא that states the same reading.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר's reading of ״אשר תאכל האש את העולה״
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי חנניא בר מניומי from the school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב

steps.title: Everyone agrees on an extra arrangement on יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: Despite their disagreements, all the Tannaim agree that on יום הכיפורים an extra arrangement is added.
steps.simpleTranslation: At any rate, everyone holds that they add [an arrangement] on that day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to point out what all opinions agree on: an extra arrangement is added on יום הכיפורים. This sets up the next question about where they learn it from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנאים argue about how many arrangements there are on a normal day. Still, all agree that on יום הכיפורים one more is added. Its purpose is to provide coals for the קטורת brought into the קודש הקדשים. Since everyone agrees, the גמרא will now look for the source they all share.

keyTerms.meaning: everyone (all opinions)
at any rate, at least
they add
on that day (יום הכיפורים)

phrases.english: At any rate, everyone
holds that they add [an arrangement] on that day.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִיהַת מוֹסִיפִין בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם אִית לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the separate verse readings to a point all the תנאים share.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All opinions agree an additional arrangement is added on יום הכיפורים.

steps.title: Where do they learn the extra arrangement from
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what verse is the source for the extra arrangement on יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the agreed rule. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of the verses about the altar fire have already been assigned other jobs. So the גמרא must find a verse that every opinion can use for the extra arrangement.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do they know this?

phrases.english: From where do they [derive it]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the agreed rule stated in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse that teaches the extra arrangement on יום הכיפורים

steps.title: It comes from the extra letters in the word for 'and the fire'
steps.stepSummary: The source is ״והאש״. Even those who do not normally learn from an extra ו (meaning 'and') do learn from the pair ו and ה (meaning 'and the').
steps.simpleTranslation: They derive it from 'And the fire.' And even one who does not expound a vav does expound 'vav-heh.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra arrangement is learned from the word ״והאש״ ('and the fire'). It adds that this works for every opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse could have said just 'אש' (fire), but it says ״והאש״, adding a ו and a ה. Some Tannaim do not learn anything from a lone extra ו. All of them, however, learn something from the extra pair ו and ה together. That is why this source works for 'everyone.'

keyTerms.meaning: they derive it
expounds, learns a rule from
the letters ו and ה ('and the')

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase ״ואו הא דריש״ does not mean 'the vav, this one he expounds.' It names two letters, ו and ה. A lone ו is not expounded by everyone, but the extra ו and ה together are.

phrases.english: They derive it from 'And the fire.'
And even one who does not expound a [single extra] vav,
does expound 'vav-heh' [i.e., 'and the'].
phrases.notes: The extra ו and ה together.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra arrangement on יום הכיפורים comes from the extra ו and ה in ״והאש״, which all opinions expound.
steps.whatToRemember: The extra arrangement on יום הכיפורים is learned from ״והאש״. Every opinion accepts this source because all of them learn from the extra ו and ה together.

steps.title: What does the phrase 'a perpetual fire' teach
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what job is left for the phrase ״אש תמיד״.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A perpetual fire' — what does it come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks for the purpose of another fire verse, ״אש תמיד״. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every phrase must have a purpose. Since the extra arrangement already has a source, the גמרא asks what ״אש תמיד״ adds.

keyTerms.meaning: a perpetual (continual) fire
what does it come to teach?

phrases.english: 'A perpetual fire' — what does it come to teach?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After a source is found for the extra arrangement, the גמרא asks about the remaining phrase.

steps.title: The incense arrangement must be on the outer altar
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from ״אש תמיד תוקד על המזבח״ that the second arrangement, which supplies coals for the קטורת, may only be on the outer altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for what was taught: 'A perpetual fire shall be kept burning on the altar; it shall not go out.' This teaches about the second arrangement, the one for incense, that it may only be on the outer altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. ״אש תמיד״ teaches where the second arrangement, the one for the קטורת coals, must be placed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the coals for the קטורת could be burning on the inner golden altar itself. The verse says 'on the altar,' meaning the same altar where the regular fire burns, which is the outer one. So the קטורת arrangement must be on the מזבח החיצון, and the coals are carried inside from there.

keyTerms.meaning: it is needed for
for that which was taught in a ברייתא
the second arrangement (for the קטורת coals)
the outer altar (the copper altar in the courtyard)

steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes assigning a job to every fire verse. It also sets a practical rule: the coals for the קטורת are always taken from the outer altar.

phrases.english: It is needed for that which was taught:

phrases.aramaic: ״אֵשׁ תָּמִיד תּוּקַד עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ לֹא תִכְבֶּה״ —
phrases.english: 'A perpetual fire shall be kept burning on the altar; it shall not go out' —

phrases.aramaic: לִימֵּד עַל מַעֲרָכָה שְׁנִיָּה שֶׁל קְטוֹרֶת
phrases.english: this teaches about the second arrangement, that of incense,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא אֶלָּא עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן.
phrases.english: that it should be only on the outer altar.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״אש תמיד״ teaches that the second arrangement, for the קטורת coals, may only be on the outer altar.
steps.whatToRemember: Each fire verse has its own job. ״אשר תאכל האש״ is about returning offering parts. ״והאש״ teaches the extra arrangement on יום הכיפורים. ״אש תמיד״ teaches that the קטורת arrangement is only on the מזבח החיצון.

steps.title: Where must the fire for the coal pan and the מנורה come from?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for the source that the fire for the מחתה and the מנורה must come from the outer altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know the rule for the fire of the coal pan and the מנורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא opens a new question. It is setting up a search for a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 showed that the coals for the daily קטורת must come from the outer altar. Now the ברייתא asks whether the same rule applies to two other fires. One is the coal pan used for the קטורת on יום הכיפורים. The other is the fire used to light the מנורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Coal pan. On יום הכיפורים the כהן גדול uses it to carry coals inside for the קטורת.
The golden candelabrum in the היכל
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: The fire of the coal pan and the Menorah, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: This means: from where do we know that their fire must come from the outer altar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the outer-altar rule from Step 8 to new cases
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that the fire for the מחתה and the מנורה must come from the outer altar

steps.title: Logical comparison: like the daily incense, use the outer altar
steps.stepSummary: The word אש appears both by the daily קטורת and by the מחתה and מנורה. Just as the קטורת fire comes from the outer altar, so does theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: It can be figured out by logic. 'Fire' is said about the daily incense, and 'fire' is said about the coal pan and the מנורה. Just as the incense fire comes from the outer altar, so too here it comes from the outer altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא first tries to answer with reasoning. It compares the new cases to the daily קטורת because the word 'fire' is used for all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daily קטורת already has a known rule: its fire comes from the outer altar (Step 8). Since the same word אש is used for the מחתה and the מנורה, the ברייתא wants to give them the same rule. At this point this is only a suggestion, and it is about to be tested.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a logical conclusion; we can reason it out.
The outer altar in the courtyard, where the fire burns all the time
Just as there, so too here. This is the standard wording of a comparison.

phrases.english: And it is logical:
'fire' is said regarding the incense,
and 'fire' is said regarding the coal pan and the Menorah —
just as there, it is from the outer altar,
so too here, from the outer altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first, reason-based answer to the question in Step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Compare to the daily קטורת: the fire comes from the outer altar

steps.title: A competing comparison: use the altar nearest to it
steps.stepSummary: The same comparison can be read a different way. The daily קטורת takes fire from a nearby altar, so the מחתה and מנורה should also take fire from the altar near them, which is the inner altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or go this way: 'fire' is said about the incense, and 'fire' is said about the coal pan and the מנורה. Just as there the fire comes from what is near it, so too the coal pan and the מנורה take fire from what is near them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back on its own reasoning. It shows that the same comparison could lead to the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison does not tell us which shared feature to copy. Maybe the feature to copy is 'outer altar.' Or maybe it is 'the closest fire.' For the מנורה and the מחתה, the closest fire is the inner altar, not the outer one. Since logic points both ways, logic alone cannot decide.

keyTerms.meaning: Or go this way. It introduces an equally strong opposite line of reasoning.
From what is near to it

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not say the הלכה is the inner altar. It only shows that the earlier logic is not strong enough by itself to decide the question.

phrases.english: Or, go this way:
'fire' is said regarding the incense,
and 'fire' is said regarding the coal pan and the Menorah —
just as there, it is from what is near to it,
so too the coal pan and Menorah, from what is near to it.
phrases.notes: For them, the nearby altar is the inner altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undermines the logical comparison in Step 10 by offering an equally valid opposite comparison
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reason-based comparison in Step 10, not the final halacha
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison is ambiguous. It is unclear whether to copy 'outer altar' or 'nearest altar.'

steps.title: The verse decides: the מנורה's fire comes from the outer altar
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק ״אש תמיד תוקד על המזבח״ teaches that the 'continual fire' (the מנורה) must be lit only from the top of the outer altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'A continual fire shall burn on the altar; it shall not go out.' The 'continual fire' I told you about may only come from the top of the outer altar.
steps.whatsHappening: Since logic could go either way, the ברייתא brings a פסוק to settle it. The פסוק decides the case of the מנורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תמיד is also used for the מנורה (״להעלות נר תמיד״). So the פסוק ״אש תמיד״ is read as referring to the מנורה's fire, and it says that fire is 'on the altar,' meaning the outer altar. This removes the 'nearest altar' option for the מנורה. It is part of the same ברייתא quoted in Step 8 to answer Step 7's question about ״אש תמיד״.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches. It introduces a פסוק that decides the question.
Continual fire. Linked to the מנורה's 'נר תמיד.'
On the top of the altar

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the common pattern: when two logical comparisons cancel each other out, only a פסוק can decide.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:

phrases.aramaic: ״אֵשׁ תָּמִיד תּוּקַד עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ לֹא תִכְבֶּה״ —
phrases.english: 'A continual fire shall burn on the altar; it shall not go out' —
the 'continual fire' that I told you about,
phrases.notes: This refers to the מנורה's נר תמיד.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא תְּהֵא אֶלָּא בְּרֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן.
phrases.english: shall be only from the top of the outer altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the deadlock between Steps 10 and 11 with a פסוק
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״אש תמיד״ teaches that the מנורה's fire comes from the outer altar

steps.title: The מנורה is solved, but what about the coal pan?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק only taught about the מנורה. The ברייתא asks for the source for the מחתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have learned the rule for the מנורה's fire. From where do we know the rule for the coal pan's fire?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא notices that one case is still open. It is setting up one more derivation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תמיד links the פסוק only to the מנורה. So the מחתה of יום הכיפורים still has no source, and the ברייתא must find one.

keyTerms.meaning: We have learned

phrases.english: We have learned the fire for the Menorah;
the fire for the coal pan, from where?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the open question to the מחתה after Step 12 solved the מנורה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that the מחתה's fire must come from the outer altar

steps.title: A proposed comparison: the coal pan is like the מנורה, so outer altar
steps.stepSummary: The word אש appears by the מחתה and by the מנורה. Just as the מנורה's fire comes from the outer altar, so does the מחתה's.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is logical: 'fire' is said about the coal pan, and 'fire' is said about the מנורה. Just as there it comes from the outer altar, so too here it comes from the outer altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tries to answer by logic. It compares the coal pan to the מנורה, whose rule was just fixed by a פסוק. This proposal is tested in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא now proposes comparing the מחתה to the מנורה, whose rule was just fixed by a פסוק in Step 12. Since the word אש appears in both, the מחתה would take its fire from the outer altar too. This is still only a proposal. The next step challenges it with a competing comparison, and Step 16 settles the question with a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Upon; from on top of

steps.whatToRemember: All three fires must come from the outer altar: the daily קטורת (from ״אש תמיד״ in Step 8), the מנורה (from the פסוק ״אש תמיד״ in Step 12), and the מחתה (from ״מלפני ה׳״ in Step 16, not from this comparison to the מנורה, which Step 15 challenges).

phrases.english: And it is logical:
'fire' is said regarding the coal pan,
and 'fire' is said regarding the Menorah —

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן עַל גַּבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן,
phrases.english: just as there, it is from upon the outer altar,
so too here, from the outer altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 13 by comparing the מחתה to the מנורה rule set in Step 12
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Proposed only: the fire for the מחתה, like the fire for the מנורה, would come from the outer altar. The final source is ״מלפני ה׳״ in Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Proposed by logic: compare the מחתה to the מנורה, so its fire comes from the outer altar. This proposal is challenged in step 15.

steps.title: A competing comparison points the מחתה to the inner altar
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא pushes back on the comparison to the מנורה. Instead, it compares the מחתה to the daily קטורת, which takes fire from the altar near it. That would mean the מחתה takes fire from the inner altar, which is near it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or go this way instead. The word 'fire' is said about the daily קטורת, and the word 'fire' is said about the מחתה. Just as there the fire comes from the altar near it, so too here the fire should come from the altar near it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges the comparison it just proposed by suggesting a different comparison that leads to the opposite answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 14 the מחתה was compared to the מנורה, which gives the outer altar. Here the מחתה is compared to the daily קטורת instead. The daily קטורת takes fire from the altar closest to it, so the מחתה should do the same, and the altar closest to the קודש הקדשים is the inner altar. Since two comparisons now pull in opposite directions, comparison alone cannot decide the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Go this way instead; a phrase that introduces a competing line of reasoning
It was said here ... and it was said there; the setup for comparing two פסוקים that share a word
From the place near it
Just as there ... so too here; the formula that carries a rule from one case to another

steps.confusionAlert: This looks like Step 11, but it is not a repeat. Step 11 argued about the מחתה and the מנורה together. Here the ברייתא challenges only the מחתה derivation from Step 14 by comparing it to the daily קטורת instead of the מנורה.

phrases.english: Or go this way:
'Fire' is stated regarding the daily incense,
and 'fire' is stated regarding the coal pan —
phrases.notes: This refers to the יום הכיפורים pan for the קטורת.

phrases.english: just as there, it is from the place near it,
phrases.notes: The daily קטורת takes its fire from the outer altar, which is nearby.

phrases.english: so too here, from the place near it!
phrases.notes: For the מחתה, that would be the inner altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a rival comparison that undercuts the comparison to the מנורה in Step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the shared word אש with the מנורה is enough to settle the source of the מחתה's fire.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word אש could just as easily link the מחתה to the daily קטורת, and that link points to the nearby inner altar.

steps.title: The words 'from before ה׳' prove it is the outer altar
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק settles the question. The מחתה's coals come 'from upon the altar from before ה׳'. Only the outer altar is partly, but not fully, 'before ה׳', so the פסוק must mean the outer altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And he shall take a pan full of coals of fire from upon the altar from before ה׳.' Which altar is partly before ה׳ but not entirely before ה׳? You must say it is the outer altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא stops arguing by comparison and brings a פסוק that decides the question clearly in favor of the outer altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מִלִּפְנֵי means 'from the part that is before ה׳'. That wording suggests only part of the altar is 'before ה׳'. The inner altar stands entirely inside the היכל, so all of it is 'before ה׳'. Only part of the outer altar lines up with the entrance of the היכל, so the פסוק must be describing the outer altar.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches; introduces a direct proof from a verse
From before ה׳; here it implies only part of the altar is 'before ה׳'
Part of it
You must say; introduces the only possible answer
The outer altar, in the courtyard

steps.whatToRemember: The מחתה's fire comes from the outer altar. The proof is the phrase ״מִלִּפְנֵי ה׳״, which fits an altar that is only partly 'before ה׳'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows why the ברייתא needed a פסוק. When two comparisons lead to opposite results, only a direct פסוק can decide.

phrases.english: The verse states:
'And he shall take a pan full of coals of fire'
'from upon the altar from before the Lord',
which altar is partly before the Lord
but not all of it is before the Lord —
phrases.notes: The inner altar is entirely inside, so all of it is 'before ה׳'.

phrases.english: you must say this is the outer altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the conflict between the two comparisons by bringing a decisive פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase ״מִלִּפְנֵי ה׳״ shows that the coals come from the outer altar, which is only partly 'before ה׳'.

steps.title: Why the פסוק needs both phrases: the first reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that both ״מֵעַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״ and ״מִלִּפְנֵי ה׳״ are needed. With only ״מֵעַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״, we would think it means the inner altar, so the פסוק adds ״מִלִּפְנֵי ה׳״.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary to write 'from upon the altar', and it was necessary to write 'from before ה׳'. If the תורה had written only 'from upon the altar', I would have said: which altar? The inner altar. So the תורה wrote 'from before ה׳'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why the פסוק uses two phrases. It begins with the first one: why ״מִלִּפְנֵי ה׳״ is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״מֵעַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״ on its own does not say which altar is meant. In the context of entering the קודש הקדשים, we might assume the inner altar. ״מִלִּפְנֵי ה׳״ removes that mistake by pointing to the outer altar.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
I would have thought; introduces the mistaken assumption
The inner, golden altar inside the היכל

phrases.english: And it was necessary to write 'from upon the altar',
and it was necessary to write 'from before God',
for if the Merciful One had written only 'from upon the altar',
I would have said: what is 'altar'? The inner altar,
so the Merciful One wrote 'from before God'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After using the פסוק as proof, the גמרא explains why each of its phrases is needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״מִלִּפְנֵי ה׳״ is needed so we do not think ״מֵעַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״ means the inner altar.

steps.title: The second reason begins: why 'from upon the altar' is needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts the second half. If the פסוק had said only ״מִלִּפְנֵי ה׳״, we would have thought the coals must come specifically from the part of the altar facing ה׳. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had written only 'from before ה׳', I would have said it must be specifically from the part that is before ה׳...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its explanation of why ״מֵעַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״ is also needed. This idea finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only ״מִלִּפְנֵי ה׳״, we might limit where the coals can be taken. We would think they must come from the exact spot of the altar facing the היכל entrance, which is its western side. The גמרא will next show how ״מֵעַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״ removes this limit.

keyTerms.meaning: Specifically; only this exact way
And if

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only 'from before God',
I would have said: specifically from the part before God,
phrases.notes: This means the side of the altar directly facing the היכל entrance. The thought continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second half of the explanation that both phrases are needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With only ״מִלִּפְנֵי ה׳״, we would wrongly limit the coals to the part of the altar facing ה׳. The resolution follows on the next amud.
